Upcoming Tournament

25th Bagby Memorial Tournament

Charles Bagby (1903-1975) was a San Francisco lawyer and chess master. He won the Mechanics’ Institute Chess Club championship in 1932, the Northern California Championship in 1949 and 1950, and the California Championship in 1958. In 1940, Bagby was elected to the Mechanics’ Institute Board of Trustees, on which he served until he died in 1975. He serving longer than any Trustee in the Institute's history. Before the establishment of the USCF rating system, regional rating systems were used. Charles Bagby was considered a master on the Northern California Chess Rating system. In 1939, Bagby played A.J. Fink, one of California’s strongest players at the time. At the Mechanics’ Institute, Bagby played International Master George Koltanowski, drawing their two games 1-1.

Tournament Rules

  • Forfeit time: 40 minutes
  • We provide clocks and set it up for players.
  • Games are US Chess regular and quick rated (so called dual-rated.)

  • What do the time controls mean?
    Time controls tell you how much time you have for each game.
    G40;d5 means game in 40 minutes with a 5-second delay on each move. This means you get 40 minutes, your opponent gets 40 minutes, and at each move the clock counts down from 5 to 0 before the player's time starts. If a player doesn't use up the whole 5 seconds, the remainder of that time is lost.

  • How many games/rounds?
    The 4SS before the time control means it is a Swiss System tournament with four rounds, or four games, that a player can play in the tournament. The tournaments are never eliminated, so win or lose, you can stay in the tournament. 

Sick Policy:
The Mechanics' Institute Chess Club asks that any player who is feeling unwell withdraw from the tournament to help protect the health of others. The club reserves the right to deny entry to players who appear visibly ill. Players who withdraw due to illness before the start of the tournament will receive a full refund as a credit to their Jumbula account.


Mechanics' Institute Chess Club reserves the right to update any details of this event (including but not limited to sections, time control, round times, prize fund, etc.) as we get closer to the event date to ensure an excellent tournament experience for players.
